summary: Adds new values to the IANA registry of digest algorithms used by Instance Digests in HTTP, and updates earlier values. Instance digests provide a checksum of a whole representation of a resource. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: HTTP Instance Digests provide a hash of a resource representation. This document adds SHA-256 and SHA-512 to the registry and updates references for existing entries.

questions: which hash algorithms for http digest
how does http verify downloaded files
subtitle: Adds SHA-256 and SHA-512 to HTTP's Instance Digest algorithm registry.

tldr.problem: The registry for HTTP Instance Digest algorithms needed additional choices and updated references.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5843 adds SHA-256 and SHA-512 and updates the MD5 and SHA entries, including their base64 encoding references.
tldr.outcome: The registry now includes the two additional algorithm names; this document is Informational and makes no other protocol changes.

today: RFC 5843 is an Informational RFC and is not listed as obsoleted or updated by the work-unit metadata.

sections.title: Instance Digests in HTTP
sections.content:
An HTTP Instance Digest is a digest, also called a checksum or hash, of an entire representation of the current state of a resource. This feature is unrelated to HTTP Digest Authentication.

The registry established by RFC 3230 lists the algorithm values used for these digests. RFC 5843 updates some existing entries and adds two more.
sections.plainLanguage: An Instance Digest is a hash of a whole resource representation. It is different from HTTP Digest Authentication.

sections.title: Updated and Added Algorithms
sections.content:
The RFC updates the MD5 and SHA registrations to clarify references, including the use of base64 encoding for their output. The SHA entry is described as the SHA-1 algorithm.

It adds SHA-256 and SHA-512, also with base64-encoded output. The RFC gives an example of a SHA-256 digest in a Digest header.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry keeps MD5 and SHA-1 and gains SHA-256 and SHA-512. The listed output encoding is base64.

sections.title: Security and Registry Changes
sections.content:
The security considerations are the same as those in RFC 3230. RFC 5843 does not describe new security rules for calculating or using an Instance Digest.

All other previous registry values remain valid. The changes described here update references and add SHA-256 and SHA-512.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC refers readers to RFC 3230 for security considerations. It leaves other existing registry values valid.
